A debater was assigned to defend one of two responses to a question ("my response") and to argue against
the other ("the other response"). Read the debater's argument below and decide which of these it does:

- "defends": it argues that its own response is correct.
- "concedes": it says or clearly implies that the other response is correct, or that its own response is wrong.
- "unclear": it does neither clearly.

# Argument

My response is correct: the polytropic calculation leads to option (C), \(-1.73\times10^6\ \text{ft-lb}_f\).

For 1 lb-mol, \(R=1545\ \text{ft-lb}_f/(\text{lb-mol}\cdot ^\circ R)\). The question gives \(273^\circ K\), which must be converted: \(273\ \text{K}=491.67^\circ R\). Also \(P_1=1\ \text{atm}=2116.2\ \text{lb}_f/\text{ft}^2\). Thus \(V_1=nRT/P_1=(1)(1545)(491.67)/2116.2\approx359\ \text{ft}^3\). For \(k=1.4\), \(10^{(k-1)/k}=10^{0.285714}\approx1.9307\), and the work magnitude is approximately \(P_1V_1(1.9307-1)/(1.4-1)\approx(759{,}600)(2.3268)\approx1.77\times10^6\ \text{ft-lb}_f\), negative for compression, so about \(-1.73\times10^6\), matching (C).

The other response mishandles the temperature by taking 273 as if it were already in Rankine, giving \(V_1=199.2\ \text{ft}^3\). It also has a sign/arithmetic error: \([421{,}547-882{,}455]/(-0.4)\) is \(+1{,}152{,}270\), not \(-1{,}152{,}270\). Therefore its jump to (J) is not justified.
